hyps.why: Upgrading edge 0 to a 3x3 conv gives much larger gains when the direct 0->3 edge is a weak skip than when it is already a conv.
With a weak pooling edge 5, the extra capacity on edge 0 matters more than when edge 5 is already a conv.
Replacing edge 4 with pooling hurts much more when edge 3 is only a skip, leaving little learnable capacity into the output.
With edge 3 removed, edge 4 is a main path to the output and degrading it is costly.
Making edge 3 a skip when edge 5 is also a skip leaves the output with almost no learnable convolution paths.
Removing edge 5 costs less when edge 4 is a strong 3x3 conv that can carry the output.
Removing edge 1 when edge 2 is none disconnects much of the cell, causing a large accuracy drop.
A conv on edge 2 adds more when its input from edge 1 is a parameter-free pooling edge than when it is already a conv.
Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv adds a new path, which is more beneficial than swapping an existing op.
Swapping pooling for skip loses less than replacing a learnable conv with skip on edge 2.
